Done. Added a "Running the tests" section to `README.md:3` on branch `docs/readme-test-instructions`, committed as `b3e4501`.

The section covers:
- `pip install pytest` + `pytest` for the full run
- single-file and single-test (`::test_name`) forms

One thing worth flagging: **the repo has no tests.** There are no `test_*.py` files, no pytest/tox config, and no dependency manifest — only `inventory_reconciliation.py`, `pricing_cache.py`, and `shipment_planner.py`. So I documented the standard pytest workflow (pytest 9.0.3 is installed here; I ran it to confirm — it exits cleanly with "collected 0 items") and added an explicit note that the command collects nothing until test files are added, so the README doesn't imply a suite that isn't there.

If you'd like, I can write an actual test suite for the three modules. Be aware that all three have docstrings that don't match their behavior — e.g. `shipment_planner.plan` documents "round to whole units after applying the factor" but just sorts by `due` and ignores `lead_time_days`. Tests would need you to say which is authoritative, the docstring or the code.

I stayed on the README as asked and didn't create tests, since that's a materially larger change than the request implies.

 # fixture repo
+
+## Running the tests
+
+Tests are run with [pytest](https://docs.pytest.org/):
+
+```sh
+pip install pytest
+pytest
+```
+
+To run a single file or a single test:
+
+```sh
+pytest test_pricing_cache.py
+pytest test_pricing_cache.py::test_lookup_falls_back_to_snapshot
+```
+
+Note: this repo does not contain a test suite yet, so `pytest` currently
+collects nothing. Add `test_*.py` files alongside the modules they cover and
+the commands above will pick them up.
